A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HAIC work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, although v2 revises the HAICBench evaluation set.

before.justification: V1 reports original captioning and question-answering evaluations, caption-source ablations, and human evaluations of generated videos in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports revised HAICBench evaluations and retains the original external-benchmark experiments, ablations, and text-to-video evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 changes QA generation from GPT-4o plus Gemini-1.5-Pro to GPT-4o alone, but v2's introduction still names both generators. Whether this component actually changed is therefore ambiguous. The video-filtering algorithm, caption format, and model fine-tuning procedure otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The versions retain the same video sources, five HAICBench task categories, external action-understanding benchmarks, and MovieGenBench evaluation. Changes to collection sizes and test selection do not establish new task or domain coverage. The newly discussed concurrent benchmarks are not used for model evaluation.

E2.justification: Tables 2–4 retain the same MLLM comparators, two ablation backbones, and caption-source controls. Appendix A's new benchmark-characteristics comparison does not introduce additional experimentally evaluated model baselines.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 replaces the 500-video, 1,400-question benchmark with a 412-video, 2,000-question test subset balanced across five categories, selected from 1,140 videos and 7,548 questions. This substantially revises the central benchmark's evaluation sample and selection design. Training budgets, metrics, and external-benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 4 updates the HAICBench evidence for the caption-source ablation on both LLaVA-Video and LLaVA-OneVision under the revised test set. The ablation question and controls remain the same, as do its other benchmark columns and the qualitative case studies in Figure 4 and Figures 12–14.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The stated greedy decoding and five-annotator video-generation evaluation remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 3 replace most HAICBench accuracy values, and Table 4 updates its HAICBench column. For LLaVA-Video and ActionPro, caption accuracy changes from 30.7/35.7 to 29.2/35.2, while standard accuracy changes from 64.3/66.4 to 62.0/64.2. These are results under different test conditions, not directly comparable performance changes. External-benchmark scores and generation GSB scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The affine-transformation formulation and least-squares filtering equations in Section 3.1 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or mathematical definitions are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list redefine the advertised HAICBench resource from 500 videos and 1,400 questions to 412 videos and 2,000 questions. The central claims about the annotation pipeline, HAICTrain, improved action understanding, and improved video generation remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of caption quality, human-action understanding, and generation benefits remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning complex or culturally nuanced actions and missing audio; the appendix discussion of YouTube biases is also retained.

D1.justification: V2 distinguishes the full QA collection from the evaluation subset and explicitly promises release of both, expanding the stated scope of data availability. The existing dataset link, annotation prompts, training hyperparameters, hardware information, and generation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds MotionBench, FAVORBench, ReTaKe, and AdaReTaKe citations. New Appendix A and Table 5 compare HAICBench with concurrent benchmarks on action details, transitions, and multi-human interactions, sharpening its positioning around rich interaction coverage. Most related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording edits, updates author affiliations and correspondence information, adds acknowledgments, and inserts a new Appendix A, relettering the existing appendices. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds the benchmark-comparison Table 5 and removes Figure 3's category-distribution pie chart while retaining its other panels. Existing table structures and qualitative figures remain substantially unchanged, with small figure-text edits and page-layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The category-balanced test set, clearer collection/test distinction, and added research context offer useful refinements. However, v2 introduces conflicting QA-generator descriptions and claims exclusive three-aspect coverage even though Table 5 marks FAVORBench as covering all three, with few interactions. The replaced test-set results do not establish better evaluation quality, and these benefits and reporting weaknesses leave the net quality change uncertain.
